messages:
maya: Heads-up — noticed a big hit-rate drop after yesterday's canary autoscale. Deploy warmers supposedly ran but new pods still have almost empty KV caches. Anyone else see this?
aj: Which cache? prefix/KV or full-response cache? numbers pls.
sasha: KV prefix cache for serving runtime (model=gpt-neox-20b-quant). I pulled metrics: cluster-wide prefix hit-rate ~72% pre-scale, then plummeted to ~14% during the scale event on the new nodes for ~12m.
maya: Logs: warmer job finished with exit 0, but warmers were hitting /warm endpoint on the service mesh and got 200s. No KV put ops in node logs. Suspect keying mismatch.
ram: Interesting — do we have a difference between warmer key generation and runtime key hashing? Warmer uses normalize_prefix(prompt) -> sha256; runtime uses sha256(user_id + prompt) for tenancy. That would explain fragmentation.
aj: If true, warmers populate keys without tenant salt, so they aren't visible to tenant-scoped runtime. We instrumented key schema last quarter but didn't enforce it in warmers. My bad.
sasha: Quick mitigation: patch warmers to accept --tenant-id flag and run per-tenant for affected customers. But that's expensive at scale. Alternative: make runtime fallback try unsalted keys for prewarm window.
perf-bot: alert at 2026-03-01T22:03Z -> KV miss spike on cluster ix-rt-3 during scaleup; avg token latency +35% for 8m.
maya: Both options have tradeoffs. Running per-tenant warmers = costy. Runtime fallback feels safe if we bound it to first 5 minutes post-node-create. We need to avoid stale collisions.
ram: Proposal: 3-step experiment:
1) Warmers produce both salted and unsalted keys (idempotent) for 5m after deploy.
2) Autoscaler hook triggers targeted warmers for the exact shard that got new nodes (only top 200 prefixes by QPS).
3) Add a scheduled daily passive warmer job that replays top prefixes with realistic length distribution to keep cold-start windows short.
aj: +1. Also we should profile warmers to identify kernel selection and batching overhead. Current warmers send serial single-requests which cause the runtime to pick small-batch kernels and not populate KV in the same way as real traffic. We should send micro-batches that mimic production concurrency.
sasha: Good call — warmers should mimic batching heuristics: vary seq-len and concurrency. Example warmer payload snippet: ```
POST /warm
{
  "model": "neox-20b-quant",
  "prefixes": ["How do I...", "Summarize:", "Translate:"] ,
  "concurrency": 8,
  "batch_size": 16,
  "tenant_id": "TBD"
}
```
maya: Also note kernel selection: during warmers we should keep sequence lengths hitting the long-path kernels (e.g., 512-1024) since those populate larger KV caches and choose different GEMM kernels. Our profiler shows that warmers using only short sequences didn't trigger the same kernel instantiation, leading to unrepresentative performance and misses.
ram: For autoscaler integration: add a post-scale hook that triggers a one-shot warmer that pulls the top-200 prefixes from recent-traffic service and pushes them with the new-node IPs as target. Keep rate low so we don't blow quota.
aj: Implementation detail: use `deploy-bot` event stream to annotate new node ids; warmers use that to set `X-Target-Node`. Example header: `X-Target-Node: ip-10-2-3-45` to bias routing.
deploy-bot: noted — will add a small event payload on scale events: `{"event":"node_add","node_ip":"...","scale_group":"..."}`.
sasha: We should also add traces in runtime to log when cache key generation falls back or misses salted->unsalted variants so we can measure effectiveness. Add a metric `kv.warmer_key_match` with labels (salted|unsalted|both).
perf-bot: experiment metric baseline -> kv.prefix_hit_rate pre-experiment: 0.71, during-scale median: 0.18.
maya: Next steps: (1) aj to patch warmers to emit both key variants + batching change, (2) ram to add autoscaler hook and target header, (3) sasha to add runtime fallback and metrics, (4) perf team to run A/B on canary pool. Can we ship a small patch today to reduce immediate pain?
aj: I can push a small change (emit unsalted variant) today and roll to canary. Will post PR.
ram: I'll prototype the autoscaler hook by EOD.
sasha: I'll add metric and a short dashboard + alert on kv.warmer_key_match < 0.5.
maya: Thanks — appreciate quick turnaround. :thumbsup: If the canary shows improvement we'll schedule a wider rollout and formalize the scheduled warmers job.
aj: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/warmers/pull/421 (WIP) — includes micro-batching and tenant flag.
maya: Great. Let's sync if we see unexpected perf regressions after changing warmers (kernel selection/batching might change steady-state).
